title: Colimit assembly over a directed cover of a simplicial diagram
statement: Use universes, simplicial subsets, nerves, coherent functors, cocones and colimits from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, let $I$ be a small nonempty partially ordered set in which every finite subset has an upper bound, and let $(K_i)_{i\in I}$ be simplicial subsets of $K$ with $K_i\subseteq K_j$ for $i\leq j$ and $K=\bigcup_{i\in I}K_i$. Let $\mathcal E$ be an infinity category admitting all small colimits and let $p:K\to\mathcal E$ be a coherent diagram. For each $i$, choose a colimiting cocone on $p|_{K_i}$ with apex $c_i$. The chosen cocones assemble to a coherent diagram $c:N(I)\to\mathcal E$, with transition maps induced by restriction of cocones, and to a compatible cocone on $c$ with apex $\operatorname{colim}_K p$. This last cocone is colimiting; in particular $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}c_i\simeq\operatorname{colim}_K p$. The assertion includes $K=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4, Remark 4.2.3.9 and Corollary 4.2.3.10, printed pp. 249-253; directed union of simplicial subsets is precisely the case described in Remark 4.2.3.9.

proof.text: Work in a universe containing the small sets $K$ and $I$. For any diagram $a:L\to\mathcal E$, write $J_a$ for the join slice of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. Its vertices are maps $L^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ extending $a$. The comparison identifies initial vertices with colimiting coherent cocones and identifies its fixed-apex fibers with the spaces of coherent cocones, naturally under restriction. Represent each prescribed local cocone by an initial vertex $q_i$ of $J_{p|K_i}$, keeping its apex equal to $c_i$: essential surjectivity of the comparison on that fixed-apex Kan fiber supplies the representative and an equivalence to the prescribed cocone. Equivalences preserve initiality because they induce equivalences on mapping spaces. These equivalences allow transport back to the prescribed cocones at the end. Likewise choose a global colimiting join cocone $\lambda$ on $p$ with apex $C=\operatorname{colim}_Kp$, which exists by the assumed small-colimit completeness. All shapes used below are small; no colimit over a category of all small diagrams is taken.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.5, Corollary 4.2.1.7, and the setup of Proposition 4.2.3.4, printed pp. 241-242, 249.

proof.text: We will use the following elementary boundary calculation. If $D$ is a quasicategory and $s:\Delta^n\to D$ has initial first vertex, then $J_s\to J_{s|\partial\Delta^n}$ is a trivial Kan fibration, including $n=0$. Indeed a lift against $\partial\Delta^m\subseteq\Delta^m$ amounts to extending a map from $(\partial\Delta^n\star\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^n\star\partial\Delta^m)=\partial\Delta^{n+m+1}$ to $\Delta^{n+m+1}$; its first vertex is $s(0)$. Pass to opposites, using the opposite quasicategory and reversed mapping-space equivalences in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. The boundary now has last vertex terminal, so [lem-cbc-terminal-boundary-extension] supplies the extension. This gives every boundary lift, including $m=0$, exactly as required in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. The same terminal-boundary criterion in opposites says directly that any $\partial\Delta^n\to D$ with initial first vertex extends when $n\geq1$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.3.3, printed p. 249; its proof is the displayed join-boundary identification.

proof.text: Define a small simplicial subset $H\subseteq K\star N(I)$ as follows. It contains the pure copies of $K$ and $N(I)$; a mixed simplex $\sigma\star(i_0\leq\cdots\leq i_r)$ belongs to $H$ precisely when $\sigma\in K_{i_0}$. Removing an initial-block vertex preserves this condition since $K_{i_0}$ is a simplicial subset; removing the first final-block vertex preserves it since $K_{i_0}\subseteq K_{i_1}$. Degeneracies preserve it as well. For $Y\subseteq N(I)$ let $H_Y$ consist of $K$ and the simplices with final block in $Y$. Well-order the cells in each dimension and filter $N(I)$ by its nondegenerate simplices after their boundaries, using [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells]. For a new vertex $i$ the new part is $K_i^{\triangleright}$ attached along $K_i$; extend $p$ by the chosen $q_i$. For a new positive-dimensional simplex $i_0<\cdots<i_n$, the new part is $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n$ attached along $K_{i_0}\star\partial\Delta^n$. The already specified map is a boundary in the quasicategory $D=J_{p|K_{i_0}}$, whose first vertex is $q_{i_0}$, initial by step 1. The boundary extension from step 2 fills it. Continue over the small skeletal filtration, taking unions at limit stages. This constructs $q:H\to\mathcal E$ restricting to $p$ on $K$ and to $q_i$ on every $K_i^{\triangleright}$. Set $c=q|_{N(I)}$. In particular, the mixed simplices for $i\leq j$ exhibit $c_i\to c_j$ as the map induced by the colimiting cocone $q_i$ and the restriction of $q_j$; higher chains give their coherent compatibilities. More explicitly, write $e_i$ for the equivalence in the fixed-apex cocone space between the comparison of $q_i$ and the prescribed cocone. The edge $i\leq j$ gives a coherent triangle from the comparison of $q_i$, via $c_i\to c_j$, to the restriction of the comparison of $q_j$. Concatenate its compatibility path with $e_i^{-1}$ at the source and $e_j|_{K_i}$ at the target. This gives compatibility with the prescribed cocones. The higher simplices of $q$ and the same equivalences supply the higher compatibilities; the apex diagram $c$ is unchanged.

source.place: Notation 4.2.3.1 and Proposition 4.2.3.4, construction in its proof, printed pp. 248-250.

proof.text: For this $q$, restriction $R:J_q\to J_p$ is a trivial Kan fibration over $\mathcal E$. Use the same filtration $H_Y$ as in step 3. At a cell $i_0<\cdots<i_n$, the already chosen map on $K_{i_0}\star\Delta^n$ is a simplex $s:\Delta^n\to D=J_{p|K_{i_0}}$ with initial first vertex $q_{i_0}$. Restriction on join slices across that cell is the pullback of $J_s\to J_{s|\partial\Delta^n}$ in $D$. By the defining simplices of the join slice in [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], both lifting problems specify the same map on $K_{i_0}\star(\Delta^n\star\Delta^m)$ and the same prescribed boundary. Step 2 makes it a trivial Kan fibration; $n=0$ treats the vertex cells. A boundary lift across the entire tower is obtained recursively by these cell lifts, keeping the previously specified lift at every successor and taking its union at limits. Thus the definition of trivial Kan fibration applies to $R$ itself. Lift the vertex $\lambda\in J_p$ along $R$ to a join cocone $\widetilde\lambda$ on $q$; since $R$ is over $\mathcal E$, its apex is the same $C$. For any apex $T$, the pullback $R_T$ on strict fibers is also a trivial Kan fibration (the same lifting square with constant apex). By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] it is a homotopy equivalence. By the fixed-apex and naturality assertions of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], restriction therefore gives an equivalence of coherent cocone spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(H,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_HT)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(p,\Delta_KT)$, compatible with postcomposition by maps out of $C$. Since composition with $\lambda$ identifies the latter space with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(C,T)$ by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], composition with $\widetilde\lambda$ identifies the former with that mapping space. Consequently $\widetilde\lambda$ is colimiting for $q$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.4, second assertion and its proof, printed pp. 250-251; fixed-apex interpretation by Corollary 4.2.1.7.

proof.text: For a simplex $\sigma$ of $K$, let $I_\sigma=\{i\in I:\sigma\in K_i\}$ with its induced order. It is nonempty because the $K_i$ cover $K$, and it is upward closed because the cover is monotone. Given two members, any upper bound in $I$ is again a member. In a poset parallel arrows are equal, so its identity arrow coequalizes every parallel pair. Thus [lem-cbc-filtered-nerve-weak-contractibility] shows $N(I_\sigma)$ is weakly contractible. Now well-order the cells in each dimension and filter $K$ by nondegenerate simplices after their boundaries. For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ form $H(L)$ using the same mixed-simplex rule with initial block in $L$, retaining all of $N(I)$. We have $H(\varnothing)=N(I)$ and $H(K)=H$. Adding a nondegenerate $m$-simplex $\sigma$ of $K$ attaches $\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$ along $\partial\Delta^m\star N(I_\sigma)$. To check the pushout, a mixed simplex with new initial block is uniquely a simplex of the characteristic $\Delta^m$ together with a chain all of whose entries contain $\sigma$; a boundary initial block is already in $H(L)$, and the pure final block is already in $N(I)$. Characteristic-map identifications on faces are made by that attaching map. If the initial block is degenerate, membership in each $K_i$ is equivalent to membership of its nondegenerate ancestor (apply degeneracies in one direction and a degeneracy's face retraction in the other); the mixed simplex is then degenerate in $H$. There are therefore no extra degenerate-initial-block cells. The cited boundary-cell decomposition supplies all the nondegenerate cells. Each attaching inclusion is right anodyne by [lem-coef-contractible-join-right-anodyne]. Closure under pushouts and transfinite compositions in [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] now shows $N(I)\hookrightarrow H$ is right anodyne.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3.8, its nondegenerate-simplex attaching argument, and Remark 4.2.3.9, printed pp. 252-253; inclusions eliminate the extra degenerate-lift case.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to $N(I)\hookrightarrow H$, $q$, and any vertex $T$ of $\mathcal E$. It identifies the space of cocones on $q$ with that on $c=q|_{N(I)}$, naturally in $T$ and compatibly with postcomposition. Restrict $\widetilde\lambda$ to get a compatible cocone $\nu$ on $c$ with apex $C$. Steps 4 and 5 give equivalences induced by composition with this very cocone, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(C,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(H,\mathcal E)}(q,\Delta_HT)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal E)}(c,\Delta_{N(I)}T)$. The cocone/initial-object criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] proves that $\nu$ is colimiting. Hence its apex $C$ realizes $\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}c_i\simeq\operatorname{colim}_Kp$. If $K=\varnothing$, all $K_i$ are empty and the construction gives $H=N(I)$: steps 2-4 apply to the chosen initial objects $c_i$, while step 5 has no cells and the final inclusion is the identity. Thus this case is covered without an unstated nonemptiness hypothesis on $K$ or on the $K_i$.

source.place: Corollary 4.2.3.10 and Remark 4.2.3.9, printed p. 253, with the cocone-space form of finality.

proof_origin.place: Explicit reconstruction of HTT 4.2.3.4 and 4.2.3.8-4.2.3.10, with the fixed-apex comparison 4.2.1.5/4.2.1.7; HTT is not archived locally, so marked agent per the standing brief.
